8e8ce998c3655b59.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants two things: the app fixed, and compensation for the hassle. The file shows no promise of any kind. Contact centre agents told her to reinstall the app and then to clear the cache. One note says an IT ticket may have been raised but that it is unclear whether it was sent. The complaints handler logged the case as a complaint. Nothing in the file shows the bank promising a fix date, compensation or any other outcome. Any redress must be decided by an authorised person.

c94a8eec3c1750b3.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: Key rules: CH-1 (dissatisfaction with inconvenience, so it is a complaint). CH-6 Medium severity: fourth contact about the same issue (repeated service failure); no loss amount is in the file. CH-7 root cause likely Systems or app failure. ESC-1: app failure needing technical investigation goes to Digital Operations, handed over within 2 business days (ESC-2) with all ten ESC-3 fields; several are MISSING (app version, evidence, IT ticket status, contact preference). CH-4/CH-5: final response by 2026-12-15, On track. VUL-2: missed rent and a 40-minute branch trip are possible indirect signs; the file does not show she was asked, so ask her sensitively. Redress is for an authorised person (CH-8, RED-5).
